t: You're at the site of the Carlton Hotel, a luxury hotel that operated from 1899 to 1940. It was designed by C. J. Phipps as part of a larger development that included the rebuilding of His Majesty's Theatre next door. The Swiss hotelier César Ritz ran it at first, with Auguste Escoffier as head chef, and it drew customers away from the Savoy. The American businessman Anthony N. Brady died here in 1913. He was once the largest shareholder in the American Tobacco Company.
